      local size = getVectorSize(vectorAddr)

      if not size or size < 1 then return false end

      local firstOpcode = readInteger(vectorAddr)
      local lastOpcode = readInteger(vectorAddr + (size - 1) * 4)

      if lastOpcode ~= opcodeContext:getOPEnumFromInternalOPID(GDFunc.OP.OPCODE_END) then return false end

      return true
    end

    local function validateFunctionConstVector(vectorAddr)
      local size = getVectorSize(vectorAddr)

      if not size or size < 1 then return false end

      local tested = math.min(size, 4)

      for i = 0, tested - 1 do
        local variantAddr = vectorAddr + i * sizeOfVariant
        local variantType = readInteger(variantAddr)

        if not isValidVariantType(variantType) then return false end
      end

      return true
    end

    local function validateFunctionGlobalVector(vectorAddr)
      local size = getVectorSize(vectorAddr)

      if not size or size < 1 then return false end

      local tested = math.min(size, 4)

      for i = 0, tested - 1 do
        local stringNameAddr = readPointer(vectorAddr + i * GDDEFS.PTRSIZE)

        if isNullOrNil(stringNameAddr) then return false end
        if isInvalidPointer(stringNameAddr) then return false end

        local name = getStringNameStr(stringNameAddr)

        if name == '??' then return false end -- TODO: could it be a mess?
      end

      return true
    end

    local function findFunctionVectorOffset(funcAddrs, validator, excludedOffsets)
      local bestOffset
      local bestHits = 0
      local scanEnd = 0x280

      for candidateOffset = 0, scanEnd, GDDEFS.PTRSIZE do
        if excludedOffsets and excludedOffsets[candidateOffset] then goto continue end

        local hits = 0

        for _, funcAddr in ipairs(funcAddrs) do
          local vectorAddr = readPointer(funcAddr + candidateOffset)
          if validator(vectorAddr) then hits = hits + 1 end
        end

        if hits > bestHits then
          bestHits = hits
          bestOffset = candidateOffset
        end

        ::continue::
      end

      local requiredHits = math.min(2, #funcAddrs)

      if bestHits < requiredHits then return nil end

      return bestOffset
    end

    local function assumeGDFuncOffset(scriptAddr)
      if hasValidGDFuncOffsetOrder() then return true end

      if not assumedOffsets.FUNC_MAP then return false end
      if not assumedOffsets.VARIANT_VECTOR_SIZE then return false end
      if not GDFunc then return false end

      local funcAddrs = collectGDFunctionAddresses(scriptAddr)

      if #funcAddrs == 0 then return false end

      local excluded = {}

      if not assumedOffsets.FUNC_CODE then
        assumedOffsets.FUNC_CODE = findFunctionVectorOffset( funcAddrs, function(vectorAddr) return validateFunctionCodeVector(vectorAddr, GDFunc.CurrentDisassembler) end )

        if assumedOffsets.FUNC_CODE then
          excluded[assumedOffsets.FUNC_CODE] = true
          sendDebugMessage( 'Valid GDFunction Code offset 0x' .. numtohexstr(assumedOffsets.FUNC_CODE) )
        end

      else
        excluded[assumedOffsets.FUNC_CODE] = true
      end

      -- func code is absolutely essential
      if not assumedOffsets.FUNC_CODE then return false end

      if not assumedOffsets.FUNC_CONST then
        assumedOffsets.FUNC_CONST = findFunctionVectorOffset( funcAddrs, validateFunctionConstVector, excluded )

        if assumedOffsets.FUNC_CONST then
          excluded[assumedOffsets.FUNC_CONST] = true
          sendDebugMessage( 'Valid GDFunction Const offset 0x' .. numtohexstr(assumedOffsets.FUNC_CONST) )
        end
      else
        excluded[assumedOffsets.FUNC_CONST] = true
      end

      if not assumedOffsets.FUNC_GLOBALS then
        assumedOffsets.FUNC_GLOBALS = findFunctionVectorOffset( funcAddrs, validateFunctionGlobalVector, excluded )

        if assumedOffsets.FUNC_GLOBALS and not hasValidGDFuncOffsetOrder() then
          assumedOffsets.FUNC_GLOBALS = nil
        end

        if assumedOffsets.FUNC_GLOBALS then
          sendDebugMessage( 'Valid GDFunction Globals offset 0x' .. numtohexstr(assumedOffsets.FUNC_GLOBALS) )
        end
      end

      return hasValidGDFuncOffsetOrder()
    end

  -- FUNC STRUCT END

  local function assumeSampleOffsets(sample)
    local nodeAddr = sample.nodeAddr

    if not assumedOffsets.SCRIPT_INSTANCE then
      assumeScriptInstanceOffset(nodeAddr)
    end

    sample = makeNodeSample(nodeAddr)

    if isNullOrNil(sample.scriptAddr) then return end

    assumeScriptNameOffset(sample.scriptAddr)

    if not assumedOffsets.SCRIPT_NAME then return end
    if GDDEFS.MONO then return end

    if GDDEFS.MAJOR_VER >= 4 then
      assumeVariantMapOffset(sample.scriptAddr)

      if assumedOffsets.VARIANT_MAP then
        assumeVariantVector(nodeAddr) -- we have means to validate the vector with map size
        assumeConstMapOffset(sample.scriptAddr) -- we have a starting point for constants
      end

      assumeFuncMapOffset(sample.scriptAddr) -- reliable, seems to work fine without enforcing var-func boundaries for const map

      if assumedOffsets.FUNC_MAP and assumedOffsets.VARIANT_VECTOR_SIZE then
        assumeGDFuncOffset(sample.scriptAddr)
      end
      return
    end

    -- 3.x
    assumeFuncMapOffset(sample.scriptAddr)

    if not assumedOffsets.FUNC_MAP then return end
    assumeVariantMapOffset(sample.scriptAddr) -- func map is in-between the const and variant maps
    assumeConstMapOffset(sample.scriptAddr) -- this makes the assumption more reliable

    if assumedOffsets.VARIANT_MAP then
      assumeVariantVector(nodeAddr)
    end

    if assumedOffsets.FUNC_MAP and assumedOffsets.VARIANT_VECTOR_SIZE then
      assumeGDFuncOffset(sample.scriptAddr)
    end
  end

  local function assumeNodeOffsetsDeep()
    clearAssumedOffsets()

    if not assumeChildrenOffset() then
      reportFailedOffsets()
      return false
    end

    assumeObjNameOffset()

    -- collect samples for continuous gdscript analysis
    local rootNodes = getMainNodeTable()
    local nodeSamples = collectNodeSamples(rootNodes)

    local maxPasses = 4

    for pass = 1, maxPasses do
      local before = offsetCount()

      for _, sample in ipairs(nodeSamples) do
        assumeSampleOffsets(sample)

        -- if collected all, stop
        if allOffsetsResolved() then
          reportFailedOffsets()
          return true
        end
      end

      local after = offsetCount()

      -- No milestone was discovered during this pass.
      if after == before then break end
    end

    reportFailedOffsets()
    return allOffsetsResolved()
  end

  -- EVIDENCE ORCHESTRATION START
    -- refactored from assumption logic with ai; allegedly inferior precision, but let it be for now

    local function recordCandidates(category, candidates, sample)
      for _, candidate in ipairs(candidates or {}) do
        recordCandidate(category, candidate, sample)
      end
    end

    local function collectUniqueScriptSamples(nodeSamples)
      local samples = {}
      local seenScripts = {}

      enrichScriptSamples(nodeSamples)

      for _, sample in ipairs(nodeSamples) do
        if isNullOrNil(sample.scriptAddr) then goto continue end
        if seenScripts[sample.scriptAddr] then goto continue end

        seenScripts[sample.scriptAddr] = true
        sample.duplicateScript = false

        table.insert(samples, sample)

        if #samples >= RESOLVER_CONFIG.maxUniqueScripts then break end

        ::continue::
      end

      return samples
    end

    local function resolveStrongNodeOffsets()
      if not assumeChildrenOffset() then return false end
      if not assumeObjNameOffset() then return false end
      return true
    end

    local function resolveStrongScriptInstanceOffsets(nodeSamples)
      for _, sample in ipairs(nodeSamples) do
        if assumeScriptInstanceOffset(sample.nodeAddr) then
          return true
        end
      end

      return false
    end

    local function validateProbedSample(sample)
      if isNullOrNil(sample.scriptAddr) then return false end
      if isNullOrNil(sample.scriptInst) then return false end

      if assumedOffsets.SCRIPT_NAME then
        local stringAddr = readPointer(sample.scriptAddr + assumedOffsets.SCRIPT_NAME)
        if isNullOrNil(stringAddr) then return false end
        if readUTFString(stringAddr, 4) ~= "res:" then return false end
      end

      if assumedOffsets.VARIANT_VECTOR then
        local vectorAddr = readPointer( sample.scriptInst + assumedOffsets.VARIANT_VECTOR )
        if isNullOrNil(vectorAddr) then return false end

        local vectorSize = readInteger( vectorAddr - assumedOffsets.VARIANT_VECTOR_SIZE )
        if isNullOrNil(vectorSize) then return false end

        if vectorSize > 2000 then return false end
        if not validateVariantStride(vectorAddr, vectorSize) then return false end
      end

      return true
    end

    local function verifyProbedOffsets(holdoutSamples)
      local passed = 0
      local tested = 0

      for _, sample in ipairs(holdoutSamples) do
        if isNullOrNil(sample.scriptAddr) then goto continue end

        tested = tested + 1

        if validateProbedSample(sample) then passed = passed + 1 end

        ::continue::
      end

      if tested == 0 then
        sendDebugMessage("[PROBE] No holdout samples available")
        return false
      end

      local ratio = passed / tested

      sendDebugMessage( ("[PROBE] Holdout verification: %d/%d, %.2f"):format( passed, tested, ratio ) )

      return ratio >= 0.75
    end

    local function probeAndCommitCategory( category, assumedName, samples, probeFunction, options )
      for _, sample in ipairs(samples) do
        if isNullOrNil(sample.scriptAddr) then goto continue end

        local candidates = probeFunction(sample)
        -- recordCandidates(category, candidates, sample)
        recordFilteredCandidates(category, candidates, sample)

        ::continue::
      end

      local best = chooseBestCandidate(category, options)

      if not best then return nil end

      assumedOffsets[assumedName] = best.offset

      sendDebugMessage( "[PROBE] " .. assumedName .. " = 0x" .. numtohexstr(best.offset) )

      return best
    end

    local function probeVariantPairCandidates(sample)
      local results = {}
      local mapCandidates = probeVariantMapCandidates(sample)

      for _, mapCandidate in ipairs(mapCandidates) do
        local vectorCandidates = probeVariantVectorCandidates(sample, mapCandidate)

        for _, vectorCandidate in ipairs(vectorCandidates) do

          table.insert(results, makeCandidate(
            mapCandidate.offset,
            (mapCandidate.score or 0) + (vectorCandidate.score or 0) + 5,
            {
              mapOffset = mapCandidate.offset,
              mapSize = mapCandidate.mapSize,
              mapSizeOffset = mapCandidate.mapSizeOffset,

              vectorOffset = vectorCandidate.offset,
              vectorSizeOffset = vectorCandidate.sizeOffset,
              vectorSize = vectorCandidate.vectorSize,
            }
          ))

        end
      end

      return results
    end

    local function probeAndCommitVariantPair(samples)
      for _, sample in ipairs(samples) do
        if isNullOrNil(sample.scriptAddr) then goto continue end
        if isNullOrNil(sample.scriptInst) then goto continue end

        local candidates = probeVariantPairCandidates(sample)
        recordCandidates("VARIANT_PAIR", candidates, sample)

        ::continue::
      end

      local best = chooseBestCandidate("VARIANT_PAIR")

      if not best then return false end

      assumedOffsets.VARIANT_MAP = best.mapOffset
      assumedOffsets.VARIANT_VECTOR = best.vectorOffset
      assumedOffsets.VARIANT_VECTOR_SIZE = best.vectorSizeOffset

      sendDebugMessage( "[PROBE] VARIANT_MAP = 0x" .. numtohexstr(best.mapOffset) .. ", VARIANT_VECTOR = 0x" .. numtohexstr(best.vectorOffset) )

      return true
    end

    local function probeNodeOffsetsMilestone()
      clearEvidence()
      clearAssumedOffsets()

      if not resolveStrongNodeOffsets() then
        reportFailedOffsets()
        return false
      end

      local rootNodes = getMainNodeTable()
      local nodeSamples = collectNodeSamples(rootNodes)

      if #nodeSamples == 0 then
        reportFailedOffsets()
        return false
      end

      if not resolveStrongScriptInstanceOffsets(nodeSamples) then
        reportFailedOffsets()
        return false
      end

      local scriptSamples = collectUniqueScriptSamples(nodeSamples)
      local trainingSamples, holdoutSamples = splitSamples(scriptSamples)

      local scriptName = probeAndCommitCategory( "SCRIPT_NAME", "SCRIPT_NAME", trainingSamples, probeScriptNameCandidates, { requiredHits=2, requiredScripts=2, requiredScore=8, } )

      if not scriptName then
        reportFailedOffsets()
        return false
      end

      if GDDEFS.MONO then
        return true
      end

      if GDDEFS.MAJOR_VER >= 4 then
        probeAndCommitVariantPair(trainingSamples)

        if assumedOffsets.VARIANT_MAP then
          probeAndCommitCategory( "CONST_MAP", "CONST_MAP", trainingSamples, probeConstMapCandidates )
        end

        probeAndCommitCategory( "FUNC_MAP", "FUNC_MAP", trainingSamples, probeFuncMapCandidates )
      else
        probeAndCommitCategory( "FUNC_MAP", "FUNC_MAP", trainingSamples, probeFuncMapCandidates )

        if assumedOffsets.FUNC_MAP then
          probeAndCommitVariantPair(trainingSamples)
        end

        if assumedOffsets.FUNC_MAP then
          probeAndCommitCategory( "CONST_MAP", "CONST_MAP", trainingSamples, probeConstMapCandidates )
        end
      end

      local verified = verifyProbedOffsets(holdoutSamples)

      reportFailedOffsets()
      return verified
    end

  -- EVIDENCE ORCHESTRATION END

  local function printAssumedOffsets()
    if isNullOrNil(viewport) then
      if not resolveRootSymbol() then return {} end
    end
    assumeNodeOffsetsDeep()
    printCurrentOffsets()

    return assumedOffsets
  end

  local function printProbedOffsets()
    if isNullOrNil(viewport) then
      if not resolveRootSymbol() then return {} end
    end
    probeNodeOffsetsMilestone()
    printCurrentOffsets()

    return assumedOffsets
  end

  gd_monitor_pause = function()
    if GDDEFS and GDDEFS.Monitor then
      GDDEFS.Monitor:suspend()
    end
  end

  gd_monitor_resume = function()
    if GDDEFS and GDDEFS.Monitor then
      GDDEFS.Monitor:resume()
    end
  end

  gd_monitor_status = function()
    if GDDEFS and GDDEFS.Monitor then
      GDDEFS.Monitor:profile()
    end
  end

  gd_monitor_setCD = function(ms)
    if GDDEFS and GDDEFS.Monitor then
      GDDEFS.Monitor:setCD(ms)
    end
  end

  gd_assumeOffsets = printAssumedOffsets
  gd_probeOffsets = printProbedOffsets

  return
    {
      ok = true
    }
end

return Module -- exporting

local LATEST_SEMVER_SUPPORTED = "4.7" -- Update me to the latest supported version when support is provided

function Module.install(contextTable)
  local GDDEFS = contextTable.GDDEFS

  local function installVersionFallback(tab, lastVersion)
    local metatable = 
      {
        __index = function(table, version)
          local fallback = rawget(table, lastVersion)
          if fallback then
            print( ("[TYPES] Version %s is not defined, do that; falling back to %s") :format( tostring(version), tostring(lastVersion) ) )
          end
          return fallback
        end
      }
    setmetatable(tab, metatable)
  end

  local function defineVariantTypeProfile()
    if GDDEFS.VARIANT_TYPE_PROFILE then
      return GDDEFS.VARIANT_TYPE_PROFILE
    end

    local function cloneArray(tabl)
      local result = {}
      for i, val in ipairs(tabl) do result[i] = val end
      return result
    end

    local function insertValueBefore(list, anchor, valueToInsert)
      for i, val in ipairs(list) do
        if val == anchor then
          table.insert(list, i, valueToInsert)
          return
        end
      end
      error("insertValueBefore: anchor not found: " .. tostring(anchor))
    end

    local function insertValueAfter(list, anchor, valueToInsert)
      for i, val in ipairs(list) do
        if val == anchor then
          table.insert(list, i + 1, valueToInsert)
          return
        end
      end
      error("insertValueAfter: anchor not found: " .. tostring(anchor))
    end

    local function removeValue(list, valueToRemove)
      for i, val in ipairs(list) do
        if val == valueToRemove then
          table.remove(list, i)
          return
        end
      end
      error("removeValue: value not found: " .. tostring(valueToRemove))
    end

    local function applyPatchOnList(list, patch)
      if patch.kind == "insertValueBefore" then
        insertValueBefore(list, patch.anchor, patch.value)
      elseif patch.kind == "insertValueAfter" then
        insertValueAfter(list, patch.anchor, patch.value)
      elseif patch.kind == "removeValue" then
        removeValue(list, patch.value)
      else
        error("Unknown patch kind: " .. tostring(patch.kind))
      end
    end

    local function prepareProfileSpec(version, specs, visited)
      local spec = specs[version]
      if not spec then
        error("Unknown Variant type version: " .. tostring(version))
      end

      visited = visited or {}
      if visited[version] then
        error("Circular Variant type profile inheritance for version: " .. tostring(version))
      end
      visited[version] = true

      local resolved = { version = version, orderedTypes = nil }

      if spec.base then
        local parent = prepareProfileSpec(spec.base, specs, visited)
        resolved.orderedTypes = cloneArray(parent.orderedTypes)

        if spec.patches then
          for _, patch in ipairs(spec.patches) do
            applyPatchOnList(resolved.orderedTypes, patch)
          end
        end
      else
        resolved.orderedTypes = cloneArray(spec.orderedTypes or {})
      end

      return resolved
    end

        ["4.2"] = { base = "4.1", patches = {} },
        ["4.3"] = { base = "4.2", patches = {} },
        ["4.4"] = { base = "4.3", patches = { { kind = "insertValueAfter", anchor = "PACKED_COLOR_ARRAY", value = "PACKED_VECTOR4_ARRAY" } } },
        ["4.5"] = { base = "4.4", patches = {} },
        ["4.6"] = { base = "4.5", patches = {} },
        ["4.7"] = { base = "4.6", patches = {} },
      }

    installVersionFallback( specs, LATEST_SEMVER_SUPPORTED )

    local version = GDDEFS.VERSION_STRING
    local resolved = prepareProfileSpec(version, specs)

    local profile =
      {
        version = version,
        names = {},
        enums = {},
        ceTypes = {},
        maxType = #resolved.orderedTypes - 1
      }

    for i, typeName in ipairs(resolved.orderedTypes) do
      local enum = i - 1
      profile.names[enum] = typeName
      profile.enums[typeName] = enum
      profile.ceTypes[enum] = ceTypeByName[typeName] or vtPointer
    end

    GDDEFS.VARIANT_TYPE_PROFILE = profile
    GDDEFS.VARIANT_TYPE_NAMES = profile.names
    GDDEFS.VARIANT_TYPE_ENUMS = profile.enums
    GDDEFS.VARIANT_TYPES = profile.ceTypes
    GDDEFS.MAXTYPE = profile.maxType

    return profile
  end

  defineVariantTypeProfile()

  return
    {
      ok = true
    }
end

return Module -- exporting
```

`docs/GDUMPER_API.MD`:

```MD
# GDDumper API

This doc covers the usage of exposed API functions.

For the moment being, the doc isn't complete and features only most useful functions.

## Dumper

- `gd_initDumper(config)`
> Initializes the dumper with the passed config. The script might guess the offsets if passed as `gd_initDumped( {useHardcoded = true} )`

  > Notes:
  > 1. Use `Debug Mode` to log errors/status
  > 2. When called, the script will try to find the SceneTree/root, in case of failure - find and register the root address with a symbol called `pRoot`

- `gd_dumpNodeToAddr( parentMemoryRecord, nodeAddr, doConstantsAsWell )`
> Builds the tree for the specified node into the CE Address List (recursively)
  ```lua
  gd_dumpNodeToAddr(memrec, gd_getDumpedNode( "NodeName" ), false)
  ```

- `gd_dumpAllNodesToAddr()`
> Builds the current root tree into the CE Address List including node members and constants (both recursively)

## Objects

- `gd_getDumpedNode(nodeScriptName)`
> If a node with this nodeScript name was discovered, returns its currently discovered address. The address might be any instance of the script that's attached to the root.

- `gd_registerNodeOffsets( nodeScriptName, namespace )`
> Registers Variant offsets of the respective nodeScript name as `nodescriptname.healthfield` symbol whose value is the respective offset in the `Vector<Variant> members`.

  > Notes:
  > 1. requires a runtime object with the respective script constructed and present in the root tree
  > 2. Use case: creating consistent address tables in case script members change across versions
  > 3. Specifying namespace doesn't do anything meaningful except for adding `somenamespace.nodescriptname.healthfield` to avoid symbol collisions.

  ```lua
  gd_registerNodeOffsets('Globals') -- then some pointer may feature Globals.isGrounded
  ```

- `gd_node_registerVariantsSelectively`
> Same as `gd_registerNodeOffsets`, but registers specific fields only to avoid a fat symbol table.

  ```lua
  local fields =
  {
    "timeout",
    "isDone",
  }
  gd_node_registerVariantsSelectively( 'Globals', fields )
  ```

- `gd_getObjectName(objectAddr)`
> returns Objects class name

  > Note: be cautious for it calls a virtual method whose index might shift in some versions - the target would just likely crash

- `gd_mono_getObjectFromNode(nodeAddr)`
>returns a mono object address for the respective node address. A script must be attached to the node. Do whatever DotNet Collector API allows you to with it.

- `gd_run_subscribe( callbackName, callback )`
>subscribe a callback to run at the end of each Node Monitor run. Returns the subscriber id.

  ```lua
  gd_run_subscribe( 'OnEndNotification', function() print('shalashaska') end )
  ```

- `gd_run_getSubscriberID(callbackName)`
>returns a subscriber id for the passed callbackName. Check `gd_run_unsubscribe` for usage

- `gd_run_unsubscribe(subID)`
>unsubscribe an existing callback via its subscriber ID

  ```lua
  gd_run_unsubscribe( gd_run_getSubscriberID('OnEndNotification') ) -- no more shalashaska
  ```

- `gd_run_subscribeRegisterNode( nodeName, memrec )`
> subscribe the following node to be registered as soon as it becomes available. Passing a memrec is optional.

  > Notes: 
  >1) No need to unsubscribe, it unsubscribes once registered
  >2) if a memrec object is passed, it will become activated upon node being registered; if it's a header/group with an address, it will be filled in

  ```lua
  gd_run_subscribeRegisterNode('Globals') -- my field offset symbols will be available as soon as possible
  ```

- `gd_run_subscribeRegisterNodeSelectively( nodeName, variantNameTable, memrec )`
> does same thing as `gd_run_subscribeRegisterNode` but with selected variants only

  > Notes: 
  >1) No need to unsubscribe, it unsubscribes once registered
  >2) if a memrec object is passed, it will become activated upon node being registered; if it's a header/group with an address, it will be filled in

  ```lua
  gd_run_subscribeRegisterNodeSelectively( 'Globals' , { 'currentScene' } ) -- only currentScene will be registered
  ```

## Script

- `gd_patchFunction( funcObjAddr, patchToBytes, startPos )`
> patches the function's bytecode to the bytes passed
  ```lua
  local toPatchBytes = { 0xDEADBEEF, 0xDEADBEEF, 0xDEADBEEF }
  local originalBytes = { 0xDEADBEEF, 0xDEADBEEF, 0xDEADBEEF }
  local funcAddr = gd_getFunctionFromNode( gd_getDumpedNode('Glogal'), '_process' )
  gd_patchFunction( funcAddr , toPatchBytes ) -- startPos would default to 0
  -- gd_patchFunction( funcAddr , originalBytes ) -- restore the bytes
  ```

- `gd_getFunctionFromNode( nodeAddr, funcName )`
> gets the func from the respective node via its name (example above)

- `gd_callFunctionFromNode( nodeAddr, funcName, argTable )`
>Invokes a user-defined script function for the respective node. Note: not every Variant type is implemented

  > arguments to be passed: e.g. { type = 'STRING' , value = 'Oh hi Mark', copy = nil }
  ```lua
  local args =
  {
    { type="FLOAT" , value=100.0 },
  }
  gd_callFunctionFromNode( gd_getDumpedNode('game') , 'checkAccuracy' , args )
  ```

- `gd_recompileScript(nodeAddr, fileName)`
>Hot-reloads the Script that's attached to the Node (will affect all nodes who are attached to the same script). The new script must be attached to Cheat Engine in `Table->Add File` menu, its name must be passed to the function

  > Notes: 
  >1) Changes might be reverted with `gd_revertScript`
  >2) Do NOT add NEW member variables (globals) to the script unless you hot-reload the respective ScriptInstance(s) subsequently for them to be constructed.
  ```lua
  gd_recompileScript( gd_getDumpedNode('silly_node') , 'new_silly_node.gd' ) -- hotreload the script from the attached file
  ```

- `gd_revertScript(nodeAddr)`
> tries to reverse the changes done to the script by `gd_recompileScript`

- `gd_reloadScriptInstance(nodeAddr)`
> hotreload the ScriptInstance for the respective node address. A script must be attached to it in the first place.

  >_Note: doesn't preserve the ScriptInstance state._
  ```lua
  local nodeAddr = gd_getDumpedNode('silly_node')
  gd_recompileScript( nodeAddr , 'new_silly_node.gd' ) -- hotreload the script from the attached file, new silly has a new member variable so I ...
  gd_reloadScriptInstance( nodeAddr ) -- hot-reload this node's ScriptInstance for members to be constructed
  ```

## Node Monitor Service

- `gd_monitor_pause()` / `gd_monitor_resume()`
> suspends/resumes the service that continuously dispatches threads walking the Node tree.

  > Notes: 
  >1) This service is responsible for discovering nodes with gdscript to enable most API functions
  >2) The service may load the CPU due to myriads of memory reads which would integrate to higher CPU usage as a result
  >3) Control the wait time between these runs with gd_monitor_setCD(newCD)

- `gd_monitor_status()`
> Reports the current run iteration, previous run delta and the amount of hit nodes, e.g. `Runs: 126 Delta: 2 ms (raw 500) Nodes met: 187`

- `gd_monitor_setCD( newMS )`
> sets a wait time between monitor runs, default is 500ms. Increase the wait time when frequent runs aren't necessary.

## Misc

- `gd_printDumped()`
>prints the currently discovered nodes with a Script attached to the Lua Engine output window

- `gd_buildGUI()`
>creates a GDumper menu button if the script doesn't do that automatically - i.e. the target wasn't identified as Godot

  >Note:
  > 1. this menu lets you explore the Scene Tree via CE's Structure Dissector
  > 2. enable `GD Dissector` inside `GDumper` menu, then click `VP Struct` to build a viewport children struct and dissect them automatically.
```

`docs/GUIDE.MD`:

```MD
# How to find a root viewport address, version and offsets
The following guide works with targets that have `GDScripts` & `GDScriptInstance`s.

## C# Targets
Godot targets with `C# Script`s have different object layouts and work via mono/.net interface. If the target exposes the respective endpoints, CE would identify it as dotnet with its collector reversing CLR objects via reflection - these objects contain a `Node` reference (internal Godot object).

If the libraries in question are static (pretty much all 3.x targets) - that would make it harder, but the aforementioned internal reference in the dotnet object would be a good path to find the respective Godot `Node` object - you just have to do it with more effort.

## Viewport
The easiest and most straightforward way to obtain the root viewport address to find any runtime `Variant` struct of a `Node`'s `Vector` since any `Node` keeps a root reference by a reverse path of `Node->GDScriptInstance->Vector<Variant>`

## Vector & Variant
The size of `Variant` struct may vary between `0x18` & `0x28` depending on whether double is used for `real_t` (which is rare).

`Variant` is a struct with a `Type` `enum` & `union` aligned by 8 bytes; hence the value is offset by `0x8`, object pointers are offset by `0x10` due to their `ObjectID` (which is `std::uint64_t`) stored at `0x8`.

Godot 4.x/3.x `Types` aren't numerous, `>=39` and `27` respectively, primitive types like `FLOAT`, `INT`, `BOOL` are enumerated as 3, 2, 1 respectively.

The `Variants` we are interested in are stored in a `Vector` as continuous elements (the layout is pretty similar to `std::vector`). A `Vector`'s 1st item is pointed at in a `GDScriptInstance` object.

So if you find the first element address of the `Vector` container - substract `0x4` (3.x-4.2) or `0x8` (4.2-4.5) or `0x10` (4.5+) from its address, you get the vector size. If the `Vector` size matches what you see, i.e. the elements stored in the `Vector`, you pretty much confirmed it's the 0-th element of the container.

Take the address of the 0th `Vector` element and search for it in the target (obviously it's a heap-allocated object). Most likely you'd end with a unique address, that would be the `Vector<Variant>` field of `GDScriptInstance`
> Don't forget about the sizeof(void*) which would be 4 byte in x32 and 8 byte long in x64 targets respectively.

Now that you are inside a `GDScriptInstance`, find the preceding `vtable` (read about vtables below). The `Vector` field isn't far from it, usually less than `0x60` on x64 (usually `0x28`).

Take the base of the `GDScriptInstance` object, i.e. the address that has the vtable pointer and search for it again, you should get the `GDScriptInstance script_instance` field of a `Node` which is around `0x50-0x70` in x64 targets, you'd deduce it by finding the `Node`'s vtable.

Now that you see a `Node`'s fields, you can find the root `Viewport/Window`. Nodes and the root have an object name field (it's a `StringName` containing a pointer to a `String`), in case of root it's 'root' (`0x8`/`0x10` inside `StringName` object). The root also has a self-reference - that should suffice to deduce it.

## Game Version
If the target has a .pck file, open it with a hex editor, it starts with `47 44 50 43` magic number in hex, after the magic there would be 3 32bit numbers: major, minor, patch. If the target doesn't have it, just search the executable with a hex editor for the very same magic number.
If the .pck is encrypted, there would be a different magic and as far as I remember, it won't feature the semantic verion.

Another way to indentify the version is by scanning the app's executable, but make sure to also search the read only sections as well. Search for `Godot Engine` in ASCII to find something like `Godot Engine v4.4.1.stable.official`. You can also use a regex formula to search the string with a hex editor featuring that.

## Offsets
> offsetNodeChildren - offset to Node->children, it's an array of `Node` pointers

> offsetNodeStringName - offset to Node->object_name, it's a pointer to a `StringName` object featuring a string at 0x8/0x10

> offsetGDScriptInstance - Node->GDScriptInstance, points to an object with a vtable where the next pointer is the owner `Node` reference with a following `GDScript` reference

> offsetVariantVector - Node->GDScriptInstance->Vector<Variant>

> offsetVariantVectorSize - size preceeding the 1st element in the Vector container, exact offset varies

> offsetGDScriptName - Node->GDScriptInstance->GDScript->name, a pointer to a raw UTF16/UTF32 string data that starts with res://

> offsetFuncMap - GDScript->member_functions, it's a `HashMap` in 4.x (4 ptrs, capacity, size) use offset to the Head (second to the last ptr); in 3.x (ptr to the RBT root and sentinel after it) use root offset.

> offsetGDFunctionCode - GDScript->member_functions['funcName']->code - Vector of 4byte integers, function bytecode

> offsetGDFunctionConst - GDScript->member_functions['funcName']->constants - a Vector<Variant> with script constants, relative to code (after it in 4.x, before globals it in 3.x)

> offsetGDFunctionGlobals - GDScript->member_functions['funcName']->global_names - Vector<StringName>, relative to code (after it and constants in 4.x, before code and after constants it in 3.x)

> offsetConstMap - GDScript->constants - layout same as w/ offsetGDFunctionCode `HashMap`/`Map`

> offsetVariantMap - GDScript->member_indices - layout same as w/ offsetGDFunctionCode `HashMap`/`Map`

## vtable
If you don't know the purpose of `vtable`s, just google/ask some LLM. In a nutshell, it's how dynamic polymorphism is achieved - hence only classes with virtual methods will feature a vtable.

The important stuff is identifying one. A vtable pointer is stored at the very start of objects. It's a c-array to readonly data section of an executable, i.e. a dense table of pointers that in turn point to some place inside the .text section (executable). .rdata and .text would be 'static' relative to the base address of the executable.

If you see a vtable, it's most likely the beginning of an object - unless you are looking at an object with multiple inheritances which is generally rare.
```

`docs/MAINTENANCE.MD`:

```MD
# How to update GDDumper for new unsupported engine versions

Most initializations happen in the `initDumper(config)`. With every new minor version shipped the script needs a respective update to retain all its features.

As for new major releases - the script would likely require considerable changes to internal functions if godot internal types happen to change.

Each new minor version needs the following updates (or validation).

### Offsets for auto-resolution

- Struct offset [major.minor] versions in `getStoredOffsetsFromVersion()`
  - Essential `Object`'s offsets usually change between minor versions, thus they have to be defined
  - `DEBUG` and `TOOLS_ENABLED` releases introduce meaningful changes to object memory and vtable layouts
  - Due to `x32` apps being unpopular since the rise of Godot Engine, not all script pointer arithmetic heuristics might succeed. Feel free to reference 32bit apps, however.

- Virtual table index for `getClassName()`
  - Essential.

### SceneTree

- AOB-signatures for `SceneTree` in `GDDumperModules/GDSignatures.lua`
  - Essential for out-of-the-box usage

### Godot Engine Variant Types (essential)

- Variant [major.minor] profiles in `GDDumperModules/GDTypes.lua` + latest ver

### GD Function Disassembler

- GDFunction [major.minor] profiles in `GDDumperModules/GDFunctionStructDisassembler.lua` + latest ver
  - In case new opcodes are added, they have to be added to all respective enums and structure disassembler handlers have to be defined.
  - Essential for GDFunction disassembler to operate

### Interface

- AOB-signatures to get a pointer of `GDScriptFunction::call()` method in `GDDumperModules/GDSignatures.lua`
  - the AOB-signature has to find a hit in the `GDScriptFunction::call()` caller, it follows stdcall call conventions
  - The signature has to be marked as heavy if the calee's first argument isn't `this` but a buffer instead

- Virtual table index for `Object::callp()` in `GDDumperModules/GDHardOffsets.lua`
  - Essential for the engine API

- AOB-signatures for `GDExtensionInterfaceFunctionPtr gdextension_get_proc_address(const char *p_name)` in `GDDumperModules/GDSignatures.lua` to enable 4.x+ GDExtended Interface
  - The AOB must find the unique address of `gdextension_get_proc_address()` prologue

- AOB-signatures for `mono_getobject()` in `GDDumperModules/GDSignatures.lua`
  - Only for 3.x .NET targets, 4.x ScriptInstances reference CLR object pointers

```

            "description": [
                "In this API there are multiple functions which expect the caller to pass a pointer",
                "on return value as parameter.",
                "In order to make it clear if the caller should initialize the return value or not",
                "we have two flavor of types:",
                "- `GDExtensionXXXPtr` for pointer on an initialized value",
                "- `GDExtensionUninitializedXXXPtr` for pointer on uninitialized value",
                "",
                "Notes:",
                "- Not respecting those requirements can seems harmless, but will lead to unexpected",
                "segfault or memory leak (for instance with a specific compiler/OS, or when two",
                "native extensions start doing ptrcall on each other).",
                "- Initialization must be done with the function pointer returned by `variant_get_ptr_constructor`,",
                "zero-initializing the variable should not be considered a valid initialization method here !",
                "- Some types have no destructor (see `extension_api.json`'s `has_destructor` field), for",
                "them it is always safe to skip the constructor for the return value if you are in a hurry ;-)"
